content:
evan: quick heads-up — while running long-context smoke tests on the new kv pager changes I saw a recurring tail-latency bump (99th → ~480ms) that lines up with sustained memory pressure and a switch in the evicter from LRU->FIFO under our fallback policy. unsure if it's correctness or just thrash. attaching notes below.
maria: hmm. which workload? long-chat or streaming-gen?
evan: long-chat with 32k contexts, mixed seq lengths. sustained writes from batcher (highly bursty). p50 stable, p95 occasional, p99 spikes every ~30s.
joel: can you paste the evicter config? might be the probation window interaction with FIFO.
evan: config snippet:```yaml
kv_evict_policy: auto
kv_autofallback: true
kv_lru_window_ms: 5000
kv_fifo_reinsert: allowed
kv_probation_ms: 800
```
maria: auto means we fall back to FIFO when LRU fails to reclaim fast enough, right? that's been the default for heavy paging.
evan: correct. timeline from logs: ```
[12:03:21] evicter: pressure=0.93 policy=LRU reclaimed=1200 entries
[12:03:51] evicter: pressure=0.98 lru_reclaim_stall -> switching to FIFO
[12:04:02] runtime: pager: moved 48 pages to swap, kv_reinsert=high
[12:04:03] perf: request-id=Z12 latency=489ms p99
```
joel: that swap/move line is interesting — suggests fragmentation forces more scanning when FIFO is used, increasing CPU and lock contention. did profiler catch any hotspots?
perf-bot: quick profile summary (sampled 10s during spike): [top stacks]
- evict::scan_entries (46%)
- pager::page_move (18%)
- kv::reinsert (12%)
- serving::generate (8%)
- runtime::syscall_wait (6%)
(plain CPU time; no heap sampling in this trace)
sam: fragmentation + FIFO reinsert chain could cause O(n) behavior per eviction when many tombstones are present. We saw similar in a microbench where contiguous free runs are small.
maria: do we have repro? can we trigger on a dev node with synthetic long-context churn?
evan: yes — repro script:```bash
# run 4 workers with mixed seqs to create hotset churn
./kvworkload --workers=4 --ctx-size=32000 --write-bursty --duration=5m --policy=auto
```
repro is ~100% on a dev-gnode-2 instance.
joel: quick mitigation idea: increase lru_window_ms and add a brief cooldown before switching to FIFO, or make FIFO do bounded rescans (cap entries inspected per tick) so we don't pay full scan cost on each fallback.
sam: also consider marking recently-reinserted entries as "probation_locked" so FIFO reinsert chains skip repeated moves. That preserves FIFO semantics but avoids long reinsert storms.
maria: would that affect correctness (stale reuse)? need to ensure we don't hide a logically freed key. maybe tie probation to a generation counter so reinserted entries are re-evaluated after a short TTL.
evan: ran a quick experiment: bumped lru_window_ms=20000 and added evicter_scan_cap=500. result: p99 dropped from 480ms → ~210ms in the same workload, but total reclaimed per second dropped ~25% (more mem pressure sustained). tradeoff.
perf-bot: quick numbers (5m window):
- baseline(auto): p99=489ms, reclaimed/s=11, swap_ops=47
- lru-window+cap: p99=212ms, reclaimed/s=8, swap_ops=12
joel: good data. prefer short-term stability (reduce p99) and then iterate on correctness/perf of FIFO.
maria: can we add an observability flag that reports "reinsert-chain-length" so we can monitor in prod instead of guessing?
evan: yeah I can add metric: runtime.kv.reinsert_chain_max and runtime.kv.scan_inspected_per_tick. will pr today.
sam: follow-up: let's roll the lru_window + cap to a canary pool for 24h, monitor p99 and reclaimed rate, and if reclaimed drops too low, enable an aggressive background compact pass that defragments the slab arena.
joel: I volunteer to prototype probation_locked + generation. I can try to keep it conservative for correctness.
maria: sounds good. evan — open a rollout doc with the repro command, perf numbers, and the metric names you added. link it here when done. :thumbsup:
evan: will do. opening PR and a canary rollout proposal this afternoon. thanks all. :rocket:
